slides.say: Any function whose name starts with use is a Hook. Hooks let your components use React features.
Here the component asks for two features: state with use state, and a ref with use ref.

slides.text: State: useState, useReducer. Context: useContext. Ref: useRef. Effect: useEffect.
slides.say: Built-in Hooks come in groups. State Hooks remember data. Context reads from far away. Refs hold values that don’t render. Effects sync with outside systems.

slides.text: Performance: useMemo, useCallback, useTransition, useDeferredValue. Plus a few others.
slides.say: Performance Hooks skip work or keep the screen responsive. And there are a few more, like use I D.

slides.text: Combine built-in Hooks to build your own.
slides.say: The takeaway: a Hook is a function starting with use. Use the built-in ones, or combine them into your own.
